Hi Claire — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call highlights
- Primary goal: 8-week pilot to validate Redwood inference for clinical summarization workload (50k tokens/day).
- Economic buyer: David Lin (CIO) — engaged, expects procurement/finance sign-off before PO.
- Security asks: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption details, and an SSO integration (SAML/OIDC).
- Timeline: procurement expects vendor reviews in 2–3 weeks; pilot kickoff targeted week of Nov 16.

Open items / asks from Pacific Health
1) Procurement needs a short MSA + pilot addendum.
2) Security team wants a one-page evidence summary up front; may request a short architecture call.
3) Budget sequence: David requested an indicative pilot price and any pilot discount or credits.

Our proposed immediate next steps
- I’ll share the mutual action plan and a succinct security evidence sheet (attached).
- Ben will send pilot pricing with a recommended commercial structure (credit vs. discounted rate).
- If you confirm the timeline, we’ll prepare a pilot addendum and a DocuSign for signature.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_pacifichealth_v1.pdf, security_evidence_summary.xlsx

If that matches your notes, can you confirm procurement contact and preferred PO cadence?

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Maya — that summary is helpful and accurate. A couple clarifications from procurement/security side: 

- Procurement contact: Jenna Ortiz (procurement@pacifichealth.com). PO cadence is monthly for pilots; we typically request a short 30-day invoice term.
- Security: SOC2 report is the minimum; if you can provide a short architecture diagram showing data flow and encryption at rest/in transit, that will reduce back-and-forth. The security team is tentatively available for a 30-minute call next Wed (Nov 3).
- Pricing: David asked whether you can provide a pilot credit (one-time) or a small trial discount; he’d like to see numbers for both options.

If you can get the MAP and evidence doc updated and send pilot pricing by EOD Friday (Oct 30), we’ll share internally and confirm the Nov 3 slot.

Cheers,

Subject: Fwd: Next steps & clearance: Pacific Health procurement + security gating — exception ask

Rishi / Monica — forwarding the thread with a brief ask. 

Summary of commercial ask from the call: Pacific Health is an attractive pilot (large regional system). They want either: 
A) $15k one-time pilot credit (covers token spend) OR
B) 15% discount off our standard pilot rate for a 6-8 week pilot.

In addition, they want an SLA note in the pilot addendum referencing 99.9% availability for the service during pilot. Procurement may push for shorter invoice terms (30 days).

Why approve an exception?
- Strategic: high expansion potential if pilot proves out; CIO is engaged.
- Timing: procurement is time-boxed — we either move fast or risk them slipping to another vendor.

Request: Can we get a conditional approval to offer option A (pilot credit) as a one-time marketing concession, and agree to the SLA language limited to pilot duration only? Legal (Monica) — can you flag any dealbreakers on the SLA verbiage/credit structure? Rishi — want your go/no-go to commit to the credit now so Maya can close calendar and DocuSign.

Notes: attaching the MAP and security sheet I updated with numbers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Next steps & clearance: Pacific Health procurement + security gating — exception ask

Thanks for the crisp summary, Ben. I’m inclined to approve the pilot credit (Option A) with the following constraints: 

1) Pilot credit capped at $15k and applicable only to the initial 8-week pilot; no retroactive credits.
2) SLA language must be scoped to a best-effort availability target for pilot (we explicitly avoid full enterprise SLA commitments). Monica — if legal signs off on the limited pilot clause, we’re good to proceed.
3) Finance to accept 30-day invoice term for pilot only; for expansion we expect standard net-45.

Monica — can you review the attached pilot addendum draft and confirm any redlines by EOD tomorrow? Ben / Maya — once Monica signs off, proceed to DocuSign and offer Claire the pilot credit option in writing (include the $15k cap and pilot-only SLA language).

If anything looks risky, escalate to me immediately.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Sales
